laws: Complete original source evaluation, scalar survival/order, selected original formatting and structural witnesses are proved before preserving capture. Lost originals, equal-looking reinsertion and changed original marks cannot become a usable subset.

The new compound removes only the ordered admitted masks. The pure Core expected tree can contain retained values, but the native executor never copies that tree or reinserts retained peer text. Only desired new runs author new characters.

Joined paragraphs and supported list heads route all retained source roots in reading order into the first root, excluding those roots from structural tombstoning. The exact expected AST is verified only after the complete staged compound. A later offline update to an old joined source still routes into the surviving flow.

Protected table cells and image captions retain their owners. Intermediate text with retained peer characters stays present and suppresses an otherwise unnecessary empty-body floor. Truly emptied bodies require exactly the fresh native floors; wrong counts, visible reuse and native historical creation guards refuse atomically.

Whole selected non-text atoms containing unmasked text refuse instead of hoisting or flattening their contents. Automatic rebase also retains complete original whole-atom and structural witnesses. Existing unmasked Core range semantics remain unchanged.

Actual peer-authored X keeps the same native scalar identity through automatic preserving revision capture, Ready preview, own-writer effect commit, Undo and Redo. Capture and effect preparation leave source checkpoints unchanged. Additional native tests compare surviving identities and complete current formats across joins, list tails, cells and captions.

Capture is a pure read in read-only mode under all six policies. Creator and explicit scope remain original. The host permanently consumes the supplied namespace even after refusal. Empty collapsed masked edits retain the exact checkpoint/frame/view and Redo, and malformed masks or disabled/mixed history requests publish nothing.

Authenticated supersession remains separate from Accept. Preserving Accept retains peer text and formatting, supplies once-only accepting-user history, recovers exact Undo/Redo and returns the original immutable decision after host restart and lease renewal without another append. The rejecting policy continues to pass its original host workflow.

The masked child's stronger whole-document/native-character read set refuses later edits, including deletion/reinsertion of an equal peer character. It is not automatically rebased as a contiguous range; repeated masked capture is explicitly Unsupported. Recapture from the original before supersession, or explicitly revise the pending child after supersession; the finalized original cannot supersede again. No default policy or broad compatibility reinterpretation is introduced.

bounds.note: Existing source/schema, traversal, selected-format, historical-cut, structural, child and revision-envelope budgets also apply. Core masks refuse overlap, reordering, scalar splits, outside-range coordinates and complete-work budget overflow. No truncation or plain-text fallback occurs.
